ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that line $AB$ intersects the parabola $C\colon y=ax^2+2x+c$ at points $A(-1, 0)$ and $B(2, 3)$. If point $M$ is a moving point on the parabola above line $AB$, and a parallelogram $MANB$ is formed with $MA$ and $MB$ as two adjacent sides, when the area of the parallelogram $MANB$ is maximized, find the area $S$ of the parallelogram $MANB$ at this time and the coordinates of point $M$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 1, draw line $MH\perp x$-axis at point $H$ through point $M$, and intersect line $AB$ at point $K$.\\
Substituting the points $\left(-1,0\right)$ and $\left(2,3\right)$ into $y=kx+b$, we get
\[
\begin{cases}
-k+b=0\\
2k+b=3
\end{cases},
\]
from which we find
\[
\begin{cases}
k=1\\
b=1
\end{cases},
\]
thus $\therefore y_{AB}=x+1$.\\
Let $M$ be the point $\left(a,-a^{2}+2a+3\right)$, then $K$ is $\left(a,a+1\right)$,\\
then $MK=-a^{2}+2a+3-(a+1)=-\left(a-\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}+\frac{9}{4}$.\\
According to the properties of quadratic functions, when $a=\frac{1}{2}$, $MK$ has the maximum length $\frac{9}{4}$.\\
$\therefore \text{The maximum area of } \triangle AMB=S_{\triangle AMK}+S_{\triangle BMK}$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}MK\cdot AH+\frac{1}{2}MK\cdot \left(x_{B}-x_{H}\right)$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}MK\cdot \left(x_{B}-x_{A}\right)$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{9}{4}\times 3$\\
$=\frac{27}{8}$,\\
$\therefore$ For parallelogram $MANB$ constructed with sides $MA$ and $MB$ being adjacent sides, when the area of parallelogram $MANB$ is maximized,\\
$\text{The maximum area } S_{\text{max}}=2S_{\text{max } \triangle AMB}=2\times \frac{27}{8}=\boxed{\frac{27}{4}}$, with $\boxed{M\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{15}{4}\right)}$;
